prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 주요 아파트 실거래가 추이(2023–2024) (language ko).
Grid: 6 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "단지명" spans 1 col × 2 row; "전용면적" spans 1 col × 2 row; "2023년" spans 2 col × 1 row; "2024년" spans 2 col × 1 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "단지명" · longest unbreakable word 13px · one-line width 105px
  col 2: header "전용면적" · longest unbreakable word 45px · one-line width 60px
  col 3: header "2023년 › 최저" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 75px
  col 4: header "2023년 › 최고" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 76px
  col 5: header "2024년 › 최저" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 75px
  col 6: header "2024년 › 최고" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 76px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
An earlier design attempt for this table was rejected by independent reviewers. Their comments: your previous preferred design was rated acceptable: The four price columns are balanced and keep the comma-separated amounts intact, making year-to-year comparisons possible. Apartment names wrap heavily, and the last area value splits within its digits. | another layout was rated poor: Several price amounts split within their digits, making comparisons harder. Apartment names also wrap heavily, although the area values remain intact. | another layout was rated poor: Price amounts stay intact and the year groups are balanced, but the apartment-name column is so narrow that names read almost one character per line, obscuring the row labels and creating very tall rows. | another layout was rated bad: Many prices and area values split within their digits, while apartment names still wrap heavily. The broken numbers make the table difficult to scan reliably.
another layout was rated poor: 가격의 숫자 묶음은 유지되지만 단지명이 거의 한 글자씩 세로로 쪼개져 행이 지나치게 길고 단지별 비교가 어렵다. | another layout was rated poor: 단지명이 여러 줄로 나뉘고 일부 가격의 천 단위 숫자까지 갈라져 같은 역할의 열을 비교하기 어렵다. | another layout was rated bad: 면적의 소수와 여러 가격의 숫자가 중간에서 끊겨 값의 식별과 비교가 가장 어렵다. | your previous preferred design was rated acceptable: 가격의 숫자 묶음이 유지되고 연도별 열의 리듬도 고르다. 다만 단지명이 많이 줄바꿈되고 마지막 면적의 소수가 끊긴다.
